title: Decay rate from $q$ and $\mu_0$
html:
Proof. Decay rate from q and \mu_0

Decay rate from q and \mu_0

The torus knot T_{3,5} mediates beta decay (beta decay as crossing change, force identification). The T_{3,5} braid (\sigma_1\sigma_2)^5 inserts at the converting quark. Its 10 crossings partition into the electron trefoil (3), the neutrino unknot (0), and the nuclear re-reduction residue (7). The fundamental weak coupling is the weak vertex form factor \mathcal{W}(q), the Markov trace of the T_{3,5} braid word in H_3(q).

The decay rate is

  \Gamma_\beta(p, A)
  = 
  \frac{|\mathcal{W}(q)|^2 \cdot \mu_0}{2\pi^3}
   \cdot 
  [2]_q
   \cdot 
  |\mathcal{M}_q|^2
   \cdot 
  f(Q).

The parameter q fixes every factor:

  1. Weak vertex form factor |\mathcal{W}(q)|^2 = |\mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{Markov}}((\sigma_1\sigma_2)^5)|^2. This full 10-crossing coupling replaces the single-crossing approximation s^2 = (q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2})^2. Under the canonical Markov trace it has the closed form \mathcal{W}(q) = q^2(q^{12} + q^8 - 1)/(q^2+1)^2, with \mathcal{W}(1) = 1/4; the vanishing of the rate in the classical limit q \to 1 is carried by the q-prefactor of the rate, which is zero at q = 1, and not by the vertex factor.

  2. q-integer modulation [2]_q = q + q^{-1}. This is the categorical dimension of the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) fundamental representation. It replaces the classical weak-interaction factor of 2.

  3. q-deformed matrix element |\mathcal{M}_q|^2. This is the Markov trace ratio between parent and daughter Gröbner--Shirshov normal forms (trace ratio observable):

      |\mathcal{M}_q|^2
  = 
  s^2
   \cdot 
  \prod_{i=0}^{p}
  \left|
    \frac{\hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{par}}}{\hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{dau}}}
  \right|^2

    The Markov-traced generator volume is \hat{V}_i = z \cdot a_i + b_i (factorization theorem).

  4. Phase-space integral f(Q). The Q-value (transition energy) is the categorical action difference Q = \mathfrak{S}_q(\mathrm{par}) - \mathfrak{S}_q(\mathrm{dau}) - \mathfrak{S}_q(e). This replaces classical energy conservation (M_{\mathrm{par}} - M_{\mathrm{dau}} - m_e). The classical formula assumes d_q^2 = 0 and fails for q \neq 1. We evaluate the action of each nucleus at q via the terminal resolution of its composite link (terminal resolution). This uses the pair Skein mass formula \mathcal{S}_{ab}(q) = (q\mu_a + q^{-1}\mu_b)/(q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2}). The fifth-power Sargent rule sets f(Q) \propto Q^5 for allowed transitions.

  5. Dimensional scale \mu_0. This single free parameter converts Skein units to physical units (MeV, seconds). It represents a choice of units, not a physical parameter.

The sensitivity of the decay rate to q is

  \frac{\partial \ln \Gamma_\beta}{\partial \ln q}
  = 
  \frac{q^2 - 1}{q^2 + 1} +
  5\frac{q^2 + 1}{q^2 - 1}
   \approx  48
  \quad\text{at } q = q_0,

so a 1\% shift in q changes the decay rate by approximately 50\%. The half-life is derived from the categorical action \mathfrak{S}_q on the nuclear link, using the identical parameter q that dictates the valley of stability.
